This is a SAFETY-tier review because the change affects posted G-code.
I used the current laws from upstream main, `893e749c09f5cd8b4253e72b9f3da047c562ebc3`.

What looks good:
- The return reads the rotary angles that the post wrote. It does not assume that G49 turns an axis.
- The retract precedes the zero-angle block. The return precedes the tool change and the first X/Y traverse.
- Doosan uses its clamp helpers around an A-axis return.
- The new tests cover the same tool, a tool change, the Tormach return, and an upright program without rotary words.
- No golden, fixture, UI, dependency, or process file changes are in this PR.

- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: PASS.
- `git diff upstream/main HEAD --check`: PASS. The worktree has no file changes after the mutations.
- The first compile attempt stalled in sccache. I stopped it and ran the local checks with the cache disabled.
- All build and test commands ran in the foreground. No GitHub runner was used.

Mutations run by this reviewer:
1. Fanuc: use the base script from the PR parent. Both Fanuc tests fail because the upright section has no B0 before its first cut. Restore the reviewed script: both tests pass.
2. Doosan DNM: use the base script from the PR parent. Both Doosan tests fail for the same missing B0. Restore the reviewed script: both tests pass.

Both mutations returned exit 101 with the expected assertion. Each restored run returned exit 0.
The base scripts were used only in this local worktree. Both reviewed scripts are restored.

Finding from the quick gate of the stacked PR #3501 (base: this PR's head `f9b38a9d7`).

The step `app suites: example_catalog` fails on two tests:
- `catalog_multiaxis_indexed::regenerates`
- `catalog_multiaxis_indexed::rebuilds`

The regenerated `examples/catalog/multiaxis/indexed/indexed.nc` adds these lines after `G90 G54 G40 G49 G80` in the sections "Back pocket" and "Tilted pocket":

```
G91 G28 Z0
G90
G00 A0.
```

This is the return block of `uprightAfterTilt()` in `fanuc.cps`. The committed catalog `.nc` does not have it. Thus the catalog `.nc` must move in this PR. Check that only these six lines change.

Second read (read-only, not built) of head f9b38a9d7eebd986afef0c3c2eeb89ccd76e2cb4.

Verdict: the rotary return is safe and in the correct sequence. I found no safety blocker. I did not change a label. But one gate result is red on this head (item 6). Do not merge until the catalog `.nc` is regenerated in this PR and the `example_catalog` step is green.

## 1. When the return is written

- The return is written at the START of each section, in `startPreamble`, directly after the `G90 ... G49 G80` line (`fanuc.cps` 762-763, `doosan-dnm.cps` 819-820). No return is written at the END of a tilted section.
- The memory is `rotAt` (`fanuc.cps` 102, `doosan-dnm.cps` 139). `heldAngles` sets it only from the angle words that a block really wrote (`fanuc.cps` 981-986). `endPreamble` and `onToolChange` reset only `lastA/B/C` and `tcpmOn`, not `rotAt`. Thus the old reset does not hide the tilt. The function clears `rotAt` only after it writes the zero words (`fanuc.cps` 748).
- The script does not use the pose records of the motion stamp (#3421, #3486). It uses its own memory of the written angles. If a later stamp rule ends a tilted section at `A0 B0`, `rotAt` is zero and no return is written. That is also correct.
- Cases:
  - Upright section, same tool: return. The dump restates the tool for each section, so this case and the tool-change case use the same path (`T.. M6`, `G43 H..` after the return).
  - Upright section after a tool change: return, before `M1` and `T.. M6`.
  - Tilted section after a tilted section: return too (needless, but safe). The next section then arms `G43.4` and states all angles. This case is NOT pinned by a test (see item 6).
  - A probe or dwell section: `onSection` calls `startPreamble`, so the return is written before any motion of that section.
  - End of program after a tilted section: NO return. `onClose` writes `G28 Z0`, `G28 X0 Y0`, `M30` (`fanuc.cps` 1327-1338, `doosan-dnm.cps` 1444-1459). The machine stops tilted. This is not unsafe for this program. But the next program starts tilted. Recommend a follow-up: write the rotary zero before `M30` when `rotAt` is not zero.
  - The first section of a program after a different program left the machine tilted: a post cannot know this (`rotAt` is null at the start).

## 2. What is written and where

Fanuc, B head on `tilthead.mch`:

```
G90 G54 G40 G49 G80
G91 G28 Z0
G90
G00 B0.
(M1 if optionalStop)
T01 M6
G43 H01
S.. M3
G00 Z<clearance>
G00 X.. Y..
```

- `G49` cancels `G43.4` before the rotary move. Thus the rotation does not move the linear axes with TCP.
- The Z retract goes before the rotary move. The rotary block has no X/Y word. `xyUnknown` makes the first traverse go to the clearance Z first, then X/Y.
- `angleWord` writes only the axes that the machine has (`statesRotary`). The Doosan post on a machine with only A writes `M11`, `G00 A0.`, `M10` and no B word. This path is not pinned by a test (the PR body says so).
- With `safeRetract` G53 and no `machine.safeRetractZ`, `retractHome` writes no retract, but it gives a warning. The rotary block then follows with no retract. The warning blocks the post in `crates/app/src/posting.rs` 726, so no program is delivered. This is acceptable. A later change can also skip the rotary block in that case.
- The modal state after the return: `rotAt` is zero, `lastA/B/C` were reset by `endPreamble`, and `tcpmOn` is false. Thus a later tilted section arms `G43.4` and states all words, and `rotaryFeed` reads a known zero.

## 3. Programs without the case

- An upright-only program: `rotAt` stays null, so `words` is empty and the function writes nothing. Pinned by `an_upright_program_after_an_upright_section_writes_no_return`.
- One tilted section and nothing after it: no section start follows, so nothing changes.
- Programs with two tilted sections DO change. See item 6.

## 4. App side

- The app is not changed. `first_traverse_posed` still judges only the first operation.
- The return height is the machine reference Z (`G91 G28 Z0`) or `machine.safeRetractZ` (`G53`). It is not the section clearance. This is the safest height that the post can command. The swing at that height over the last X/Y is still not checked against tall stock or fixtures.
- Item 3 of the issue is open in #3477.

## 5. The test

- `crates/post/tests/upright_after_tilt.rs` builds the streams by hand through `post::dump` (one tilted section with a 20 degree lean, then one upright section).
- It pins for fanuc and doosan-dnm on `tilthead.mch`, with the same tool and with a tool change: a retract, then the zero word with no X/Y, then the first X/Y traverse, then the first cut. Tormach is pinned for an indexed A section.
- Not pinned: a tilted-then-tilted pair, the Doosan A-only machine, the end of the program, and mach4.

## 6. Law and gates

- Decision file, `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #3466` are present. The script has no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!`.
- The body reports `gate quick --base base-3421` (125 steps, 0 failed) and `gate heavy --base base-3421` (27 steps, 0 failed) on f9b38a9d7. The base is the head of #3421, not `main`.
- RED: the comment of 16:02Z on this PR reports that `app suites: example_catalog` fails on this head (`catalog_multiaxis_indexed::regenerates` and `::rebuilds`). The program `examples/catalog/multiaxis/indexed/indexed.nc` gets the new return in the sections "Back pocket" and "Tilted pocket". `main` has no change to that file. Thus a merge of this head makes `main` red. The body statement "Goldens moved: None" is not correct for this file. Regenerate the file in this PR, check that only those lines change, and run the step again before the merge.

## 7. Overlap with main

- `git merge-tree` with `origin/main` is clean.
- Since the merge base, `main` changed only `fanuc.cps` in `declaredOptions` and `onCycle` (rigid tap). There is no change in `startPreamble`, `endPreamble`, `retractHome` or the section start. `doosan-dnm.cps` and the test file have no change on `main`.

Coordinator, to the collaborator who set `merge-ready` on head f9b38a9d7: I set `needs-rework` and removed `merge-ready` in one step (#3382). - `app suites: example_catalog` fails: `catalog_multiaxis_indexed::regenerates` and `::rebuilds`.
- Cause: `examples/catalog/multiaxis/indexed/indexed.nc` gets the new return blocks in the sections "Back pocket" and "Tilted pocket" (a tilted section that follows a tilted section). The file on `main` does not have them. The line "Goldens moved: None" in the body is not correct for this file.

A merge of this head makes `main` red.

## Requested
1. Make `indexed.nc` again with the catalog tool in this PR, and list it under the changed programs in the body, with the reason.
2. Decide the tilted-then-tilted case on purpose: the return to zero between two tilted sections is safe but not necessary. Keep it or skip it, and pin the choice with a test.
3. Run `example_catalog` and the heavy lanes on the new head against the current `main` (the run in the body used `--base base-3421`). This PR is `P1`: the heavy result on the head comes before `merge-ready`.

Not blocking, for a follow-up: no return is written before `M30` after a last tilted section; the Doosan path with one rotary axis has no test.
